repeated row of similar motifs along a band
low-relief carving on a flat stone surface
justification: Both surfaces show profile animals in low relief organised with horizontal registers and a band of repeated motifs (rows of bucrania-like forms in A, a rosette frieze in B), and both include a humanoid figure, but these are generic conventions. A depicts schematic, flattened predators, birds and a snake stacked vertically on a narrow pillar with no interaction, while B shows a naturalistic, correctly proportioned camel led by a striding attendant holding its rope in a single continuous procession, so the specific subjects, relationships and rendering conventions diverge entirely.
